title: "Export: start, then poll"
description: Write a file from an agent, follow the job until it finishes, stop it, and read what the file holds.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

An agent's export doesn't wait for the file. `export` checks the request, puts a job on the Export Queue and answers at once, and the agent then asks how it's going until it ends.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Export…', 'Window ▸ Export Queue']}
  keys="⌘E"
  where="The export sheet's Add to Queue, and each row's Cancel in the Export Queue"
  tools={['export', 'export_status', 'cancel_export']}
/>

## Write a file

<Steps>

1. Call `export` with a preset and a path. It answers straight away.

   ```json
   { "preset": "h264", "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut", "size": "1080p" }
   ```

   ```json
   { "export_id": 3, "path": "/Volumes/Edits/cut.mp4", "status": "running" }
   ```

2. Call `export_status` with that `export_id`, pause, and call it again until `status` is `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

3. Read the `done` answer. It says what the file holds, including the loudness it measured and any warnings.

</Steps>

To stop the job, call `cancel_export`. The job shows in **Window ▸ Export Queue** like any other, but the window doesn't open by itself.

## Export

`export` does what **File ▸ Export…** does with **Add to Queue**, and it runs through the same writer, so an agent's file and a person's match. It takes the [export sheet](/export/export-sheet/)'s controls in the sheet's own terms, apart from the frame rate.

| Argument | Type | Required | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preset` | string | Yes | The encoding: a container and a codec. See [Presets](#presets). |
| `path` | string | Yes | Where to write, such as `~/Movies/cut.mp4`. See [Path handling](#path-handling). |
| `size` | string or `[width, height]` | No | The output size. See [Size](#size). |
...

title: "What an export includes"
description: "The rules every export shares: what it matches, what it waits for, how it treats missing media, graphics and captions, and what it labels."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Whichever format you pick, every export follows the same rules. This page says what ends up in the file, what an export stops to wait for, and what makes it fail.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Export…" keys="⌘E" tools="export" />

## The same picture and sound

An export uses the same composition and the same compositor as the preview, so what you see while editing is what the file holds. It always writes the whole timeline, or the [range](/export/range/) yo

View-only settings never reach the file: [Preview Quality](/timeline/preview-quality/), [Show Ungraded](/color/show-ungraded/), [Show SDR Version](/hdr/show-sdr-version/), [Show Selection](/color/show

The sound goes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, so a mix that passes its ceiling sounds louder while editing than in the file. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).

export/loudness.mdx:82:Every export of a file with sound reports what that sound measured, on the [finish line](/export/progress-and-report/#the-finish-report) 
## Waiting for what it needs

Some of what a file holds has to be made first. An export waits for all of it, and never writes that sound silent or that clip uncut. If it can't be made, the export fails and names the clip, except for a cursor track.

| It waits for | Which clips | If it can't be made |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Masks, made on this Mac | Every clip with [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) that the export draws, in GIF and Animated PNG too | "Clip 4's person masks could not be made: …" (or "foreground masks", for a picture set to Foreground) and no file is written |
| [Rendered sound](/speed/ramp-audio/) | Every speed ramp, and every clip at a constant speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off | "Clip 4's retimed audio could not be rendered: …" |
| The isolated voice | Every clip with [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | "Clip 4's isolated voice could not be rendered: …" |
| The voice effect | Every clip with a [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | "Clip 4's voice effect could not be rendered: …" |
| The clip's measured loudness and speech | Every clip with the [gate](/audio/gate/), [leveller](/audio/leveller/) or [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) on, because their thresholds follow it | See below |
| Cursor tracks | Every clip with a [recorded cursor](/recording/cursor/) | The clip draws without its cursor, the export goes on, and the finished line counts a cursor warning |

Only the loudness wait has a limit. If a measurement hasn't landed after five minutes, the export fails with "Clip 4's loudness or speech has not been measured yet, so its gate, leveller and de-esser cannot be set. Wait for their Status rows to show the clip's loudness, then export again." A clip th

While it waits, the [progress sheet](/export/progress-and-report/) reads "Preparing “Board.mp4”…", and a row in the [Export Queue](/export/export-queue/#rows-and-their-states) stays at `Writing · 0 %`. You can cancel at any point. An Animated GIF or Animated PNG has no sound, so it waits only for ma

[Save Frame](/export/save-frame/#waiting-for-masks) works differently: it waits up to 30 seconds for masks, then saves the clip whole.

## Missing media

A picture gets one mask, made once on this Mac from the picture as the preview draws it, the right way up. When it's done, **Status** goes from Analyzing to **Ready**, or to **No person found** or **No subject found**.

**Person** uses the same person segmentation as a video. **Foreground** uses the Vision framework's foreground instance mask, which keeps every foreground subject it finds. If it finds none, **Status** reads **No subject found** and the pic

## Exports

With **Background** on **Remove**, an export draws the subject alone in every frame, GIF and APNG included. It waits until every mask its range needs is made, with no time limit, and the Exporting sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name

If a mask can't be made, the export fails with "Clip n's person masks could not be made: …" and writes no file. For a picture with **Subject** set to **Foreground**, the message says "foreground masks".

A single frame doesn't wait as long. **File ▸ Save Frame…** (<kbd>⌥⌘E</kbd>) waits up to 30 seconds for the masks it needs. If they aren't ready by then, it saves the frame with the clip whole, and a sheet titled "Saved without Remove Backg
